turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen saw his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have until 4:40, so tell me who decided this and on what basis.
Thanks for coming in. I'll start with an apology: I put a zero in the gradebook on November 3 without calling you first. Our procedure says I should have called. I didn't.
Okay. Go on. Who else knows about the zero, and what is it based on?

I decided it, and so far it's me, Owen and you. It's based on the document's version history first. The doc was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with just a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, 794 more in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
Say that again slowly, Hale. Created when, and how many words arrived at 11:52?
So in under ten minutes, almost two thousand words land in two pastes. Nobody types that fast.
Hale, nobody types that fast? You're guessing about my son's typing. Did anyone ask him to paste it in or to show you his drafts first?

Created 11:31 PM, Wednesday October 28. At 11:52, 612 words. I'll print the history for you to take home. Second thing: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the Folger text, the scene is tabbed, you can search it on your phone right now.
I'll check it on my phone. A wrong quote doesn't tell me who wrote the essay, though. Did you ask Owen about that line before you wrote it down?
Did you search it?
Not yet. I'm still waiting for your answer. Did you ask Owen about the line before you entered the zero?
I didn't ask him about that line specifically. I'll answer more in a second, but please, search it now, I'll wait. Type 'kingdom in exile' into the Folger search. What comes up?
Fine. You didn't ask him, so that's on the record. I'm not doing your search for you, Hale. Read me the result, and then tell me what Owen was asked on the day you entered the zero.

Zero results. The phrase isn't in the play. On Owen: I talked with him after class on November 2, the day before the zero, about five minutes. My notes are dated that day. I asked what 'epistemological paralysis' means, the phrase his essay is built on. He said 'like, being stuck.' I asked which scene his second paragraph covered. He couldn't tell me.

Okay. That's a dated search and a dated note, and I can check both myself. I still don't accept that Owen not explaining a phrase in five minutes after class tells you who wrote the essay, so I want your notes in writing before anything else.

His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice. And his September 24 in-class piece: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations, all cited act, scene, line.

Those are dated documents I can check, so I'll stop disputing them one by one. Owen changing his argument between an outline and a final essay happens all the time, and I'm not conceding the rest. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and stays out of his class. Send me the outline, the September 24 piece and your notes, in writing, today.
I'll send all three today. And to be accurate about what I said: I talked to Owen on November 3, then entered the zero that afternoon.

Okay. Then you're telling me the zero went in the same day you spoke to him, not the day before. I'll write that down. Don't you dare call the conversation the basis for the zero unless the notes say so.

Here's what I can offer. Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'd also tell you the school's AI checker scored it 94 percent, but I don't put much weight on that.

Then put the rewrite in writing today, with "nothing goes on file" in the same sentence. It happens privately, not in front of his class, and the zero comes off the gradebook before it does. You said you don't weigh the 94 percent, so take it out of the terms.
It's 4:39, by the way. You said you had a call at 4:40.

Then I have one minute. Written terms, Hale: the zero comes off today, the rewrite is private, and nothing goes on Owen's record. I'll be checking my inbox at 9:00 tomorrow morning, and if it isn't there, I'm in the principal's office on Thursday.
Agreed. The zero comes off today, the rewrite is supervised and private, outside class time, and nothing goes on his record. You'll have it in writing tonight, with the principal copied.
Good. Send it tonight with the principal copied, and I want the three documents with it. Owen will be at the writing lab Thursday, not in your classroom. I'm going to my call.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

To: Hale
Cc: Principal
Subject: Owen Kalinowski, English 30-1 essay

Hale,

Confirming what we agreed today, November 10:
- The zero for Owen's Hamlet essay comes off the gradebook today.
- Owen completes a supervised rewrite, private and outside class time, before the December 1 deadline.
- Nothing about this goes on his record.

Please also send the October 15 outline, the September 24 in-class piece, and your November 2 notes by 9:00 tomorrow morning.

If I don't have these by then, I'm going to the principal on Thursday, November 12.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, a supervised rewrite with nothing on file, agreed in writing.
Moved at: "The zero comes off today, the rewrite is supervised and private, outside class time, and nothing goes on his record."
Slipped at: none
